subject: Consolidate DPA clause variants for EEA deployment & order form signoff
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@healthsync.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00+00:00
Subject: Consolidate DPA clause variants for EEA deployment & order form signoff

Hi all —

Quick kickoff: HealthSync is preparing to enable EEA-hosted instances for their pilot. Legal has returned a mix of redlines across three artefacts (MSA exhibits, Order Form v5, and the DPA). We need to converge on a single set of DPA clauses (SCCs + role language) that procurement can sign by end of next week.

Short asks:
- Daniel: can you confirm which EEA regions they intend to use for production? (helps with SCC selection)
- Ben / Karthik: please review the attached DPA redline draft and flag any operational blockers (KMS, subprocessor list, host regions).
- Laura: once Ben/Karthik mark up, can you review legal points we should push back on and provide a suggested clause to propose to HealthSync?

Attachments: HealthSync_DPA_redline_v3.docx (docx) — combined legal + ops redline.

Notes on scope: this is not the full MSA rework — focus on: SCCs alignment, controller/processor role mapping, data export fallback (transfer impact addendum), and a short order form amendment.

Timeline: target signoff 2026-11-10 for procurement to issue PO the week of 11/15. If any escalations needed, flag them by EOD 11/03.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@healthsync.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthSync Procurement <procurement@healthsync.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:14:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Consolidate DPA clause variants for EEA deployment & order form signoff

Thanks Naomi —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick answers:
- Regions: planned pilot in Frankfurt (eu-central-1) and Amsterdam (eu-west-1). Production footprint may add Dublin later.
- Procurement wants a short, redline-friendly order form amendment; long annexes slow approvals.

I reviewed the attached file and have two immediate concerns:
1) KMS key ownership language in section 4.2 reads like full customer-managed keys; HealthSync can accept envelope encryption but not a model that requires us to manage HSM credentials. Can Redwood provide a clear option for AWS KMS CMKs with customer access logs?
2) Subprocessor list: HealthSync requires a 15-day notice and an explicit right to object for subprocessors that will process EEA customer data. They are sensitive to any cross-border analytics vendors.

I've attached our internal redline (OrderForm_v5-track-changes.pdf).

On timing: we can try to sign a limited order form amendment while the DPA remains in parallel negotiation; procurement prefers to avoid open SCC questions but will accept a transfer impact addendum if it contains concrete fallback routing.

Best,
Daniel Park
Head of Procurement, HealthSync
[Attachment: OrderForm_v5-track-changes.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@healthsync.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:32:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Consolidate DPA clause variants for EEA deployment & order form signoff

Looping in ops notes —

Thanks Daniel for the details. Short technical takeaways from infra:
- KMS: we can offer envelope encryption where HealthSync supplies the CMK material and we keep CloudTrail logs for key usage. We cannot put HSM credentials in a shared Redwood-managed HSM that gives customers full key rotation control today; that would need a dedicated private deployment.
- Subprocessors: current list includes analytics vendor PulseSight (EU data processed outside EEA). We can add a 15-day notice + right to object clause, but objections that relate to core cloud infra (e.g., CDN edge caches) will be limited.

Proposed negotiation posture:
- Accept a compromise KMS clause (Envelope + customer-provided key referencing with audit logs) in the DPA; include an explicit path to private deployment if customer requires full CMK control.
- Add the 15-day notice + objection right to the DPA. For subprocessors that are critical infra, add a specific carveout with rationale and evidence.

Naomi / Laura: draft language below for the SCCs/roles (short snippet to use in redline):
"Redwood serves as Processor for the Service. Where Redwood operates dedicated or VPC-hosted capacity at the customer's direction, Redwood will act as Processor with customer-managed exception controls as set out in the Service Exhibit. Subprocessor notice: Redwood will provide at least 15 days' notice and an opportunity to object in writing to any new subprocessor intended to process personal data originating from the EEA. Objections are limited to material legal/regulatory grounds."

I'll mark these as tracked edits in the master doc and push back on any language that mandates HSM-based CMK handover.

-Ben
Director, Privacy Engineering

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@healthsync.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T16:45:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Consolidate DPA clause variants for EEA deployment & order form signoff

Thanks team — consolidated next steps and legal posture below.

Summary of agreed positions:
- SCCs: we will use the standard EU Commission SCCs for Controller-to-Processor with Appendix A/B filled to reflect EEA hosting locations (Frankfurt, Amsterdam; Dublin as optional).
- Roles: Redwood acknowledged as Processor; language clarified for dedicated/private deployments to expressly allow customer-managed controls where applicable.
- KMS: accept envelope encryption approach with customer-supplied CMK references + CloudTrail log delivery. Offer private deployment as an escalation path with estimated lead time.
- Subprocessors: add 15-day notice + right to object; include carveout language for critical infra with evidence.

Action items (owners):
- Ben: update HealthSync_DPA_redline_v3.docx with the clause snippets and save as v4. Track changes on KMS and subprocessor carveouts. Due: 2026-11-07 17:00 UTC.
- Karthik: prepare an Order Form amendment (short, single-page) that references the DPA v4 and includes a transfer impact addendum with routing/fallback commitments. Due: 2026-11-08 12:00 UTC.
- Naomi: prepare a brief negotiation email and proposed fallback wording for SCC-related transfer impact questions. Target: 2026-11-08 EOD.
- Daniel / HealthSync: please review DPA v4 and Order Form draft, run Procurement approval on your side. If HealthSync accepts the envelope KMS compromise, procurement can proceed with PO issuance.

I've created a DocuSign envelope for the order form interact (link below). I'll hold final legal signoff pending Ben/Karthik updates. If anything stalls, we escalate to Contracts leadership by 11/09.

DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/some-fake-envelope/0a1b2c3d
Jira PR: PRIV-8421 for internal tracking.

Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
